chapter: Black and Tan and Kansas City nightlife
title: Jam sessions with visiting bands: Goodman, Ellington and Clouds of Joy
summary: Basie and traveling bands sat in after hours at the Sunset, and Benny Goodman brought his band to listen.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Count Basie an' them's band was downtown at a nightclub, an' we was on the other side of town...colored joint. So, when they got off from work, they come out there where we was workin' at, but we stayed open later'n they did. And we'd have a jam session. Ever'body sit in and have a jam session.

We had a cat called "The Fiddler." He played the violin. He was good. But some white boy come through there, played the violin, so we had a contest. White boy outplayed "The Fiddler." He really did. So, we used to have a lot of fun like that. Different cats come in from outa town, like, uh, Stepin Fetchit, Ina Ray Hutton...mmmmn, they come to town, they work downtown at the hotels, so when they get off from work, they come out South where we worked at, so's that's how come we get a chance to meet all those people, and they come in and sit in with us... bring part of their band.
We had...Benny Goodman came in...used to get his whole band.
Did he play? Or just the members of the band?
I've heard that he used to go to jam sessions and listen but I never heard of him playing.

He never played none. He'd come there and listen to the music and bring his whole band. And Duke Ellington with his band used to come. Twelve Clouds of Joy. All the big bands used to come through Kansas City, and we invite 'em out to the nightclub. We'd have barbecue for 'em and spaghetti. Ever'body have a ball. We have a good time.
